productManagement.title: AI Product Management
productManagement.subtitle: From problem discovery to measurable product outcomes.
productManagement.statement: I don't treat AI as a feature to be added to an existing product. I start with the user problem, define the desired outcome, determine where AI creates leverage, and design the product and architecture around that outcome.

projects.name: AI Software Factory
projects.category: AI Product Engineering · Agentic Software Development
projects.problem: Software development assisted by AI can become inconsistent when requirements, context, architecture and implementation decisions are not structured.
projects.solution: An orchestration workflow that structures the path from product requirement to implementation — through specification, planning, specialist agents, validation and pull requests.
impact: Reduced friction between requirements and implementation

metrics.metric: Time from requirement to implementation-ready change

projects.name: MARK1 — AI Technical Support Agent
projects.problem: Technical support requires investigating tickets, documentation and legacy source code across disconnected knowledge sources.
projects.solution: An AI technical support agent that investigates a request across documentation, tickets and code — producing a grounded technical answer.

projects.name: Luna — Enterprise AI Knowledge Platform
projects.problem: Organizational knowledge is distributed across documents, meetings, incidents, systems and integrations.
projects.solution: A multi-tenant platform that consolidates organizational knowledge into a knowledge layer and exposes it through grounded AI agents.

projects.name: SpecKitBasic
projects.problem: AI coding assistants can generate code quickly but lack structured product context and consistent engineering rules.
projects.solution: A lightweight specification-driven methodology that adds structure, rules and context before AI-assisted implementation — the foundation behind the AI Software Factory.

projects.name: Enterprise MCP Platform
projects.problem: Enterprise APIs and business capabilities are difficult for AI agents to consume safely and consistently.
projects.solution: A platform concept that exposes enterprise APIs to AI agents through MCP, with security, governance and access control.

approach.title: How I build AI products
approach.message: AI products are not built by choosing an LLM first. They are built by understanding the problem, defining the outcome, designing the right experience, choosing the appropriate AI architecture, validating quality and measuring product impact.

measure.title: How I measure AI products
measure.disclaimer: Illustrative example — a way of thinking, not measured results.

thinking.title: How I think about AI
thinking.intro: The questions I work through when designing an AI product.

tensions.title: Agent or deterministic workflow?
tensions.body: Not every problem needs an agent. I start from the workflow and introduce an agent only when autonomy, tool use or multi-step reasoning genuinely creates value.

tensions.title: RAG or structured data?
tensions.body: The retrieval architecture follows the information problem — grounded questions need retrieval; well-defined queries may not need it at all.

tensions.title: Bigger model or better context?
tensions.body: I optimize the whole system — prompts, context, retrieval and flow — before reaching for a larger model.

tensions.title: Accuracy, latency or cost?
tensions.body: AI product decisions are product decisions. The right trade-off depends on the experience, the risk and the business value at stake.

tensions.title: Human or AI?
tensions.body: Human-in-the-loop stays wherever the business risk requires it — for review, judgment and accountability.

thinking.diagramCaption: I evaluate AI product decisions as product trade-offs, not purely technical decisions.
